newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Feb 18 - Our final estimate on CPO production in January shows a downward revision of 10,000 tonnes to 568,000 tonnes. This represents a decline of 70,000 tonnes or 11 percent compared to December. The downward revision reflected mainly poorer than expected output in Peninsular Malaysia, especially in the two leading producing states of Johore and Pahang which experienced dry weather conditions during the greater part of the month. There was little evidence of harvesting of under-ripe fruits ahead of the double festive holidays in early February.

Overall, production in Peninsular Malaysia is estimated to have dropped more than 12 percent. East Malaysia fared better when its output fell around 5 percent. In recent days beneficial rains with 30-60 percent coverage had been falling in most crop areas. This coupled with a resumption of normal operatings after the festive holidays in February 7-14 should ensure a significant recovery in production in the last 10 days of this month. In line with the downward revision in CPO production, we also lower the estimate on palm oil stocks at end-January by 10,000 tonnes to 715,000 tonnes.

CPO stocks had been scaled down to an estimated 365,000 tonnes, down from 435,400 tonnes at end December and 494,700 tonnes a year earlier. Stocks of PK/PKO at end January are estimated to have shrank some 15,000 tonnes to nearly 130,000 tonnes. The bulk of the drop in stocks was in the form of palm kernels. Kernel stocks were hardly enough to meet five days crushing requirements in January. However, as crushing margin was poor and very much in the negative, a sharp contraction in crushing activity is expected in February.

The ex-mill price of PK had retreated from 890-895 ringgit in mid-January to 840-845 ringgit this week. In contrast, the cash price of CPO remained steady to firm fluctuating mostly between 1,320 and 1,340 ringgit in last-half January and holding around 1,360 ringgit since the market reopened for trading on February 12 after the long holidays. Underpinned by the strong fundamentals, CPO futures also inched higher in the last two weeks. April futures settled at 1,316 ringgit on February 14 up from 1,302 ringgit at the start of the month.
With new export demand continuing sluggish, no significant changes in price or market direction is likely in the next two weeks or at least until the next PORLA release on Saturday February 22.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
